zh: (1133-89) king of England (1154-89). He was the grandson of Henry I, succeeded King Stephen, and was the first Plantagenet king. He reduced the power of the barons and increased the power of the state. He wanted to reduce the power of the Church, which led to his dispute with the Archbishop of Canterbury, Thomas Becket, which ended in Becket's murder. During his rule England established control over Ireland. Henry also introduced various systems of justice which can be seen as the beginning of common law.

He took back power in 1265 after a battle in which the rebels were defeated by an army led by Henry's son (later Edward I).

zh: (1421-71) king of England (1422-61 and 1470-1) and son of Henry V. He was not popular, mainly because England finally lost the Hundred Years War while he was king. Opposition to him led to the Wars of the Roses, in which the House of Lancaster was defeated by the House of York and Henry was put in prison. As a result of this, Edward became king, but in 1470, with the help of the powerful Earl of Warwick, known as Warwick the Kingmaker, Henry became king again, but he was defeated once more in 1471. He was put in the Tower of London, where he was murdered, and Edward became king again. Henry VI established Eton College and King's College, Cambridge.

zh: (1457-1509) king of England (1485-1509), the first Tudor king. Born Henry Tudor, he was brought up in France. In 1485 he led a rebellion against Richard III, defeated him at the Battle of Bosworth Field and became king. In 1486 he married the daughter of Edward, uniting the House of Lancaster (to which he belonged) and the House of York and so bringing the Wars of the Roses to an end. Although there were rebellions during his rule, including those led by Lambert Simnel and Perkin Warbeck, Henry established greater order in the country, introduced a more modern system of government and greatly improved the country's financial position.

zh: an organization that runs a public hospital for the National Health Service in Britain. The first hospital trusts were created in 1990, when the British government decided to make hospitals responsible for their own management and financial affairs. The idea was that they should be run on a more commercial basis, with less waste of money and resources. In 2004 the government introduced a new type of organization in England called the foundation trust or foundation hospital. Hospitals that achieve a high level of service can apply for foundation status, which gives them the right to raise their own finances, for example, by selling assets or borrowing money. The first twenty foundation trusts were created in April and July 2004. Many people are opposed to foundation hospitals because they believe they will create a situation where some hospitals have a lot of money and others not enough.

ex: The company opened a £15 million hypermarket at Stockton.
该公司在斯托克顿开设了一家价值1500万英镑的大型超市。

en: the condition of being long-sighted

zh: a word with a general meaning that includes the meanings of other particular words, for example ‘fruit’ is the hypernym of ‘apple’, ‘orange’, etc.
en: a word with a general meaning that includes the meanings of other particular words, for example ‘fruit’ is the hypernym of ‘apple’, ‘orange’, etc.

zh: 非常敏感的；很容易生气的
（对某些物质、药物、光等）过敏的
en: very easily offended
ex: He's hypersensitive to any kind of criticism.
他对任何批评都受不了。

zh: a medical condition that causes the body to have extreme physical reactions to particular substances, medicines, light, etc.
非常敏感的；很容易生气的
en: a medical condition that causes the body to have extreme physical reactions to particular substances, medicines, light, etc.
ex: patients with hypersensitivity to the drug
对药物过敏的患者

en: space that consists of more than three dimensions
blood pressure that is higher than is normal

zh: suffering from blood pressure that is higher than normal
en: suffering from blood pressure that is higher than normal
ex: hypertensive patients
高血压患者

en: text stored in a computer system that contains links that allow the user to move from one piece of text or document to another
ex: a hypertext link on the internet
互联网上的超文本链接

en: a condition in which the thyroid is too active, making the heart and other body systems function too fast

zh: （器官或组织的）肥大，过度生长
en: an increase in the size of an organ or tissue because its cells grow in size
to breathe too quickly because you are very frightened or excited
a condition in which you breathe too quickly because you are very frightened or excited
ex: The symptoms of hyperventilation can mimic all the symptoms of anxiety and chronic stress.
过度换气的症状可以模拟焦虑和慢性应激的所有症状。

en: the mark (-) used to join two words together to make a new one, as in back-up, to show that a word has been divided between the end of one line and the beginning of the next, or to show that something is missing (as in short- and long-term)
ex: Is there a hyphen in post-mortem?
验尸中有连字符吗？

zh: 用连字符连接；用连字符分割（词语）
en: to join two words together using a hyphen; to divide a word between two lines of text using a hyphen
ex: Is your name hyphenated?
你的名字有用连字符吗？

zh: 用连字符连接；用连字符分割（词语）
en: the act of joining two words using a hyphen; the division of a word between two lines of text using a hyphen
ex: hyphenation rules
连字符使用规则

zh: learning something while you are asleep or under hypnosis
en: learning something while you are asleep or under hypnosis
an unconscious state in which somebody can still see and hear and can be influenced to follow commands or answer questions
ex: She only remembered details of the accident under hypnosis.
她只有在催眠状态下才能记起那次事故的细节。

en: a person who uses hypnosis to treat people who have physical or emotional problems
ex: I work as a clinical hypnotherapist in a hospital.
我在医院担任临床催眠治疗师。

en: a kind of treatment that uses hypnosis to help with physical or emotional problems
ex: Hypnotherapy can be beneficial for those who wish to give up smoking or to lose weight.
催眠疗法对于那些希望戒烟或减肥的人可能是有益的。

zh: 有催眠作用的；使人昏昏欲睡的
催眠状态的；催眠状态引起的
en: making you feel as if you are going to fall asleep, especially because of a regular, repeated noise or movement
ex: hypnotic music
引人昏昏欲睡的音乐

en: the practice of hypnotizing a person (= putting them into an unconscious state)
a person who hypnotizes people
ex: She went to a hypnotist hoping he could help her to give up smoking.
她去找一个催眠师，希望他能帮助她戒烟。

en: to produce a state of hypnosis in somebody
ex: He was hypnotized by her beauty.
他见她艳丽动人而神魂颠倒。

en: under; below normal
ex: hypodermic
皮下注射的

zh: 不致过敏的；低变敏原的
en: hypoallergenic substances and materials are unlikely to cause an allergic reaction in the person who uses them
a state in which somebody worries all the time about their health and believes that they are ill when there is nothing wrong with them

zh: worried all the time about your health and believing that you are ill when there is nothing wrong with you; suffering from hypochondria
en: worried all the time about your health and believing that you are ill when there is nothing wrong with you; suffering from hypochondria
behaviour that does not meet the moral standards or match the opinions that somebody claims to have
ex: He condemned the hypocrisy of those politicians who do one thing and say another.
他谴责了那些说一套做一套的政客的虚伪。

zh: 伪君子；伪善者；虚伪的人
en: a person whose behaviour does not meet the moral standards or match the opinions that they claim to have
ex: Charles was a liar and a hypocrite who married her for money.
查尔斯是个骗子和伪君子，嫁给她是为了赚钱。

zh: behaving in a way that does not meet the moral standards or match the opinions that you claim to have
en: behaving in a way that does not meet the moral standards or match the opinions that you claim to have
ex: It would be hypocritical of me to have a church wedding when I don't believe in God.
我不信上帝却到教堂举行婚礼，那就是我的虚伪了。

zh: while behaving in a way that does not meet the moral standards or match the opinions that you claim to have
en: while behaving in a way that does not meet the moral standards or match the opinions that you claim to have
under the skin; for giving somebody an injection under the skin
ex: a hypodermic injection
皮下注射

en: the condition of having too low a level of blood sugar

zh: 下义词，下位词（如 dog 和 cat 是 animal 的下义词）
en: a word with a particular meaning that is included in the meaning of a more general word, for example ‘dog’ and ‘cat’ are hyponyms of ‘animal’

zh: 从句的使用；从属关系；主从结构
en: the use of subordinate clauses
the side opposite the right angle of a right-angled triangle

zh: 下丘脑（有调节体温、摄食、内分泌等的功能）
en: an area in the central lower part of the brain that controls body temperature, hunger and the release of hormones
a medical condition in which the body temperature is much lower than normal
ex: Elderly people may die of hypothermia if they cannot afford to heat their homes.
如果老年人无法负担得起房屋的暖气，他们可能会因体温过低而死亡。

zh: （有少量事实依据但未被证实的）假说，假设
en: an idea or explanation of something that is based on a few known facts but that has not yet been proved to be true or correct
ex: to formulate/confirm a hypothesis
提出／证实假设

en: to suggest a way of explaining something when you do not definitely know about it; to form a hypothesis
ex: The causes can be hypothesized but not proved.
原因能够被假定，但不能被证实。

en: based on situations or ideas that are possible and imagined rather than real and true
ex: a hypothetical question/situation/example
假定的问题／情况／例子

en: in a situation that is possible and imagined rather than real and true
ex: Hypothetically, this is possible, but I've never known it to happen.
从理论上讲，这是可能的，但我从未知道它会发生。

en: a condition in which the thyroid is not active enough, making growth and mental development slower than normal
a lower than normal amount of oxygen in the blood
a condition in which not enough oxygen reaches the body’s tissues

zh: an animal that looks like a rabbit but is related to the elephant and lives in desert country in Africa and Arabia
en: an animal that looks like a rabbit but is related to the elephant and lives in desert country in Africa and Arabia

zh: a small plant of the mint family, used in herbal medicine
en: a small plant of the mint family, used in herbal medicine
a medical operation to remove a woman’s womb
ex: She had to have a hysterectomy.
她必须进行子宫切除术。

zh: 大肆鼓吹；狂热夸张；大惊小怪
en: a state of extreme excitement, fear or anger in which a person, or a group of people, loses control of their emotions and starts to cry, laugh, etc.
ex: There was mass hysteria when the band came on stage.
乐队登台时观众一片疯狂。

zh: 歇斯底里的；情绪狂暴不可抑止的
en: in a state of extreme excitement, and crying, laughing, etc. without any control
ex: hysterical screams
歇斯底里的尖叫

zh: in an extremely excited way and without any control, often with crying or laughter
en: in an extremely excited way and without any control, often with crying or laughter
ex: to laugh/cry/scream/sob hysterically
歇斯底里地大笑／大哭／尖叫／哭泣

en: an expression of extreme fear, excitement or anger that makes somebody lose control of their emotions and cry, laugh, etc.
ex: He went into hysterics when he heard the news.
他听到这个消息时变得歇斯底里。

en: (in writing) hertz
(in writing) hertz

en: a US make of ice cream which is sold in many countries around the world, in some places through its own shops
